long_biography.plain_text:
At the Milhous Museum in Boca Raton, printing entrepreneur Robert Milhous assembled antique cars alongside elaborate mechanical musical instruments with his brother Paul. His enthusiasm for machinery had begun with repairing old cars as a teenager; he subsequently studied mechanical engineering and industrial economics at Purdue University. The brothers' collection brought together restored automobiles, fairground organs, clocks and a specially built carousel.

Milhous took antique cars on rallies around the world, while the museum hosted charitable events. The brothers' first collector car, a 1934 Packard Convertible Victoria, became a Pebble Beach Best of Show winner. When they dispersed the collection at auction in 2012, bidders came from eighteen countries. An Oldsmobile Limited headed the sale, setting an auction record for the marque.
